title: Nested Toy Type Inference
prompt:
Implement a small structural type language and generic return-type inference. A type node is either an atomic string or a tuple of nodes. `parse_type(text)` accepts atomic names and nested tuples written with either `()` or `[]`; empty and one-element tuples are meaningful. `format_type(node)` must use canonical parenthesized formatting.

Implement `infer_return_type(actual_params, parameter_patterns, return_pattern)`. Generic variables are atomic names matching an uppercase letter followed by optional digits (for example `T` or `A12`). Recursively unify each actual type with its matching parameter pattern. A generic has one structural binding across the whole call and may bind to a nested tuple. Substitute bindings into the return pattern.

Raise `ValueError` for malformed type text, arity or structure mismatches, incompatible repeated bindings, or an unbound generic in the return pattern. Do not mutate caller-provided nodes.

example.reasoning: Bindings are structural and may be substituted in any return position.
